analysis.title: November 2026 Market Insights: S&P 500 Monthly Excess Return, Equal Weight vs. Cap Weight
key_insights: The average S&P 500 stock (equal weight) returned +5.0% in October 2026 while the cap-weighted index fell -0.9%, a gap of about 5.9 percentage points.
The October equal-weight vs cap-weight gap was the widest since 2009 and the second largest since 1990.
Cap weight outperformed equal weight by roughly 6 to 12 percentage points annually from 2023 through 2025, so October marks a reversal of that pattern.
The report says one month is not a trend, but similar rotations in 1999 to 2002 and 2009 came as market leadership broadened.
risk_factors: One month of equal-weight outperformance is not a trend, per the report.
charts_described: Chart titled 'The Widest Weighting Gap Since 2009' plots the monthly excess return of S&P 500 Equal Weight vs. Cap Weight from 1990 to 2026, in percentage points, with the axis running from -8% to 12%.
vol_and_positioning: Equal-weight S&P 500 (+5.0%) outperformed cap-weight (-0.9%) in October 2026, a 5.9-point gap, consistent with a rotation away from the largest index constituents toward the average stock.
